_comment: Japanese target-language pack. Gameplay never reads this: CreatureState still stores the English semantic IDs ('big', 'small'), and this file only decides what the student sees and says. Keys are CATEGORY/word because English reuses one word across pairs - 'short' is HEIGHT/short (background legs) and LENGTH/short (a shorter body), which are two different Japanese words. Keying by word alone would collapse them.
_display_note: Student-facing text is kana, spaced わかちがき, because the readers are beginners and because the bundled font subset carries every kana but only some kanji - see ui/noto_sans_jp_subset_ATTRIBUTION.txt. Recognition forms below are a separate field and DO carry kanji: Chrome's ja-JP recogniser returns 大きい whether or not we ever draw it, and a transcript is compared as a string, never rendered.
_forms_note: past_forms / present_forms are surface forms accepted from the recogniser, most complete first. They deliberately include both the kanji and kana spellings and the bare inflected adjective without です, because Chrome returns short utterances unpredictably. The frame (前は / 今は) is matched separately, so it must NOT be repeated inside these.

HEIGHT/tall._note: HEIGHT changes the legs. 高い alone means expensive or high-up, so the body part is named.

LENGTH/short._note: The other 'short'. A shorter BODY, never height - see HEIGHT/short.

AGE/old._note: The one pair with no adjectival antonym: 若い has none that fits an animal, and 古い is for objects and is deliberately absent from every list here. Settled by the teacher on 年を取っています - the canonical way to say an animal or person is old. 年寄り stays only as an accepted alternate, because a child who says the simpler correct thing must not be marked wrong. Canonical forms are first: _kana_polite_form() shows the first kana polite form it finds, so order decides what the learner is asked to say.
AGE/old.display: としを とっている
past_forms: としをとっていました

STRENGTH/strong._note: Pair is hidden in the Word Lab but kept so saved creatures stay valid.

SPEED/fast._note: 速い and 早い are both はやい and Chrome returns either; both accepted.

TEMPERATURE/hot._note: 熱い is hot-to-touch, which is the creature's trait; 暑い (weather) accepted because the recogniser picks it by sound.

TEMPERATURE/cold._note: 冷たい (cold to touch), not 寒い (cold weather).

COLOR/green._note: From here down the colours are NOUNS, not i-adjectives: でした / です, never かったです. This is the split the pack exists to make explicit.
